Data was copied without the knowledge of the owner

items.x: Aryabhata, India's first satellite, was launched in 1975 by a Soviet Kosmos-3M rocket from Kapustin Yar, USSR.

items.x: ISRO's first launch-view gallery at Sriharikota (Satish Dhawan Space Centre), opened in 2019, can seat 5,000 people.

items.x: The Satish Dhawan Space Centre at Sriharikota is in Tirupati (formerly Nellore) district, Andhra Pradesh. Thumba is in Kerala, and Kulasekarapattinam (new SSLV port) is in Tamil Nadu.

PSLV type satellite launching vehicle is used to launch:

items.x: PSLV has launched remote-sensing (IRS), communication (GSAT-12, CMS-01) and navigation (IRNSS) satellites and the interplanetary Chandrayaan-1 and Mars Orbiter. Only option b contains A, C and D, so 'interstellar' is read loosely as interplanetary.

items.s:
Assertion (A) : ISRO launched a communication satellite named GSAT-31 in February 2019, successfully.

Choose the correct answer :
o: A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A

items.s: DTH television stands for:
items.x: DTH = Direct To Home: TV signals from geostationary satellites go straight to small home dishes.

items.s:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding GSLV-II

a. It was launched from Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota

b. It was launched from Kourou launch base French Guiana

c. Launch vehicle was Delta-IV

d. Launch vehicle was Ariane-5
items.x: The stem is garbled: it evidently means GSAT-11, launched on 5 Dec 2018 from Kourou, French Guiana, on Ariane-5 (b and d). A GSLV itself flies from Sriharikota, and Delta-IV is an American rocket.

items.s:
Consider the following statements in respect of India's advanced satellite INSAT-4A:

A. INSAT-4A was launched in December, 2005 from New Mexico.

B. The European commercial launch service provider Ariane space was associated with the launch of INSAT-4A.

C. Tata-Sky-a digital cable service provider is associated with DTH television broadcasting services from INSAT-4A.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
items.x: INSAT-4A was launched in December 2005 from Kourou, French Guiana (not New Mexico) on an Arianespace Ariane-5 (B), and Tata Sky's DTH service uses it (C). So B and C.

items.s: The orbit of INSAT - 1B is said to be :
items.x: INSAT-1B, like all INSAT satellites, is in a geostationary orbit.

items.s:
Consider the following statements:

B. G-Sat is communication-cum-meteorology satellite which has been launched by ISRO

C. All the SAARC Countries signed for launching G-Sat satellite
items.x: GSAT-9, the South Asia Satellite, was built by ISRO for SAARC nations (A) as a communication satellite also used for disaster and weather information (B). Pakistan did not join, so C is false.

items.s:
Consider the following:

a. Satellites move around the earth with the same speed as the Earth spins

b. Satellites cover every part of earth except poles and surrounding areas which are out of their range
o: Both a and b are true
Neither a nor b is true
items.x:
No printed key. If the stem means geostationary satellites only, both a and b would be true (option c).
Taken generally, neither holds: only geostationary satellites keep pace with the Earth's spin, and polar-orbiting satellites do cover the poles.

items.s: The period of revolution of geostationary satellite is:
items.x: A geostationary satellite completes one revolution in about 24 hours (one sidereal day), matching Earth's rotation.

items.s: By which launch vehicle was GSAT-7 'Rukmini', the Indian Navy's communication satellite, launched in 2013?
items.x: GSAT-7 was launched by Ariane-5 from Kourou in 2013.

items.s: By which launch vehicle was APPLE (1981), India's first experimental geostationary communication satellite, launched?
items.x: APPLE was launched in 1981 on Ariane-1 from Kourou. SLV-3 launched Rohini (1980); the Space Shuttle Challenger carried INSAT-1B (1983); the Vostok launcher carried IRS-1A (1988).

items.s: By which launch vehicle was INSAT-1B (1983), with which the INSAT system was commissioned, launched?
items.x: INSAT-1B went up on the US Space Shuttle Challenger; Ariane-1 carried APPLE (1981).

items.s: INSAT supports which search-and-rescue programme?
items.x: Besides telecom, TV, meteorology, telemedicine and tele-education, INSAT supports COSPAS-SARSAT search and rescue.

items.x: GSAT-30, a C/Ku communication satellite on Ariane-5, replaces INSAT-4A.

items.s: INSAT services are carried in which frequency bands?
items.x: INSAT uses the C, Ku, Ka and S bands; L5 and S are NavIC bands.

items.x: INSAT-4CR (2,130 kg) was launched by GSLV-F04.

o: The heat shield did not separate
The rocket ran of fuel before the launch

items.x: SCATSAT-1's scatterometer gives ocean wind data for weather forecasting and cyclone prediction and tracking. GSAT-31 and GSAT-7A are communication satellites, and Cartosat-2C does mapping.

items.x: JACIE (Joint Agency Commercial Imagery Evaluation) is a collaboration of US agencies (NASA, NOAA, NGA, USGS, USDA) that use and produce satellite land remote-sensing data; the other options are Indian institutes.

items.x: PARIMAN (Portal for Analytical Regional Information and Mapping of NCR) is the NIC-developed web geo-portal of the NCR Planning Board, launched in 2021 and opened to the public in July 2022.

Licensed Development Agency of the Region

items.s:

instrument to measure wind speed in snow covered regions
air to air guided 2nd generation missile for air defence

items.x: The Godavari valley coalfields are associated with Singareni, which is now in Telangana. The historical observation was that Andhra lacked coal and would draw on Singareni.

items.x: The Coal Controller's Organisation performs all three functions.

items.x: The first coal-gasification fertiliser plant is planned at Talcher, Odisha; JSPL's Angul plant is the only commercial-scale gasification plant.

items.s: What is India's rank among the world's coal producers?
items.x: India is the second-largest producer (about 10%) after China (51%); its output was 1,040.08 MT in FY 2025-26.

items.s: The Supreme Court’s cancellation of 204 coal blocks in 2014 was followed by which legislative measure for auction-based allocation?
o: Mines and Minerals Act, 1957, without amendment

items.x: Commercial mining auctions for coal began in 2020.

items.x: SCCL is a joint company of Telangana and the Centre: Telangana holds 51% and the Government of India 49%. Reversing the split is the usual trap. It is neither wholly State-owned nor majority Central.

items.s: What does the syngas produced by coal gasification mainly contain?
o: Carbon monoxide, hydrogen, methane and carbon dioxide

items.x: Coking coal mines were nationalised in 1971-72 and non-coking mines in 1973; Coal India came in 1975.

items.s: Which of the following lignite field - State pairs is correctly matched?
items.x: Neyveli lignite is in Tamil Nadu and Barmer lignite is in Rajasthan.

items.s: In January 2023, The Indian Oil Corporation started the export of its special aviation fuel for small aircraft and unmanned aerial vehicles (drones), AVGAS 100 LL. The first consignment was exported to which country?
items.x: IOC's first export consignment of AVGAS 100 LL (Jan 2023) went to Papua New Guinea.

Printed key: Tamil Nadu. Strictly: Rajasthan (Rawatbhata) has the most power reactors; among the options Maharashtra, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu each had about four in 2016 (general knowledge, not checked).

Which of the following options is correct for the given assertion and reason?
Assertion (A): India is actively promoting the use of renewable energy sources such as wind, hydro, solar, geothermal, bio, and tidal power to supplement fossil fuel-based electricity generation.
Reason (R): Renewable energy sources are sustainable and environmentally friendly unlike non-renewable sources like coal, oil, and natural gas, which are finite and contribute to environmental pollution.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
items.x: Both are true and R explains A: India pushes renewables because they are sustainable and clean, unlike finite, polluting fossil fuels. (Moved to 5:64.)

items.s: Unlike traditional asphalt, bio-asphalt is not based on fossil fuels. 2. Bio-asphalt can be made from non-renewable resources. 3. Bi-asphalt can be made from non-organic waste materials. 4. It is eco-friendly to use bio-asphalt for surfacing of the roads. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.x: Bio-asphalt is made from renewable organic matter (vegetable oils, molasses, lignin, waste), not fossil fuels, and it is eco-friendly for road surfacing. Statement 2 (non-renewable resources) is false. Statement 3 says 'non-organic' here, but the original UPSC wording is 'organic', which is why the official key is 1, 3 and 4.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
items.s: Which of the following statements is not correct about 'Mangal Turbine'?
o: The turbine provides clean alternative source of energy.
It requires low water heads upto 1 meter.
Flow of wind is the source of energy for turbine.
items.x: The Mangal Turbine (Mangal Singh, Lalitpur, UP) is driven by flowing water at low heads, not by wind. It is clean and eco-friendly and lifts water for irrigation.

items.s: Which of the following is NOT an example of bio-mass energy source?
items.x: Atomic energy comes from uranium nuclei, not from biomass. Wood and gobar gas are biomass sources, and coal is fossilised plant matter.

items.src: APPSC Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences Mains Paper-II I

Enhancing the efficiency of hydroelectric power plants
Promoting the use of natural gas for power generation

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening

items.x: Biogas is mainly methane (50-65%) with carbon dioxide (35-50%) and traces of hydrogen, nitrogen and hydrogen sulphide, so 'all of the above' is the intended answer; methane alone is only the main constituent.

items.s: Which is the major constituent of Gobar Gas?
items.x: Gobar gas (biogas) is mainly methane (50-65%), with CO2 next; ethane, butane and H2S are not the major constituent.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies

items.s: India's first ever bio-fuel flight facilitated by Council of Scientific and Industrial Research flew between
items.x: India's first biofuel-powered flight (SpiceJet, August 2018, fuel from CSIR-IIP) flew from Dehradun to Delhi.

items.s:
Microbial fuel cells are considered a source of sustainable energy. Why?

A. They use living organisms as catalyst to generate electricity from certain substrates.

B. They use a variety of inorganic materials as substrates.

C. They can be installed in waste water treatment plants to cleanse water and produce electricity
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.x:
UPSC/coaching key: (c) A and C only. Some books (e.g. the printed key here) give (d), since a few inorganic substrates such as sulphides can be used.
Statements A and C are correct: MFCs use living microbes as catalysts and can be fitted in waste-water plants to clean water while making electricity. Statement B is wrong as a reason because MFCs mainly run on organic substrates. (Moved to 5:67.)

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
items.s: The wastes discharged from a biogas plant are reused as
items.x: The slurry (digestate) left after biogas is made is a nutrient-rich organic manure, so it is reused as fertilizer for crops. It is not used as cooking fuel (the gas is), animal feed or building material.

items.src: APPSC Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences Mains Paper-II I
items.s: Which of the following is the main focus of the SATAT initiative launched by the Government of India?
items.x: SATAT (Sustainable Alternative Towards Affordable Transportation, 2018) promotes setting up compressed bio-gas (CBG) plants and selling CBG as a transport fuel; GOBARdhan builds on it. It is not a solar, EV or refinery scheme. (Moved to book 5, other renewables/biofuels.)

items.s: Which company unveiled India's first H2ICE technology for heavy duty trucks in 2023 ?
items.x: Reliance Industries, with Ashok Leyland, unveiled India's first hydrogen internal-combustion-engine (H2ICE) heavy-duty truck at India Energy Week, Bengaluru, on 6 Feb 2023.

items.s: When an environmentally sensitive person driving a car stops at a traffic light, the person would?
o: Keeps the engine on in neutral gear
Keeps the engine in gear, uses the brake and goes fast on green signal so that others would spend less fuel in waiting
Switches off the engine and turns on till green light
Does not stop at any signal because waiting and starting wastes fuel
items.x: An environmentally sensitive driver switches the engine off while waiting at a red light, saving fuel and cutting emissions; idling or never stopping is wasteful or unsafe.

items.x: Load on the phases of a DG set should be balanced; the maximum permissible unbalance between phase loads is about 10% (energy-audit guidance).

items.x: Bees get nectar and pollen while flowers get pollinated – both gain, so the relation is symbiotic (mutualism), not parasitic or predatory.

items.x: Honeybees perform the waggle dance to show direction and distance of food (Karl von Frisch).

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies

o: Search for food and suitable breeding grounds

items.src: APPSC Assistant Conservator of Forest (General Studies & Men

items.x: Concrete is a man-made material; coal, cow dung and petrol (from crude oil) are natural resources.

items.s: In lichen, a chlorophyll-containing partner, ____ live together.
o: More than one of the above
items.x: A lichen is a symbiotic association of an alga (the chlorophyll-containing partner) and a fungus. (Off-topic: ecology.)

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
items.s: What is the role of ecological succession in an ecosystem?
o: To show the energy flow through different trophic levels
To depict the rate of biomass production
To illustrate the process of decomposition
To describe the gradual process of change in the species structure of an ecosystem
items.x: Ecological succession is the gradual change in the species structure of an ecosystem over time. It is not about energy flow, biomass production or decomposition.

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
items.s: What does succession describe in an ecological community?
o: The gradual change in species composition over time after a disturbance
The daily movement of organisms within an ecosystem
The complete extinction of species in an area
items.x: Succession is the gradual change in species composition over time, for example after a disturbance. It is not migration, daily movement or extinction.

items.s:
Which of the following are the consequences of deforestation?

I. It enhanced carbon dioxide concentration in the atmosphere

II. It causes loss of biodiversity

III. It disturbs hydrologic cycle
items.x: Deforestation raises atmospheric CO2, causes biodiversity loss and disturbs the hydrological cycle – all three.

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
items.s: Wasteland refers to land with what percentage of productivity?
items.x: Wasteland is commonly defined as land whose biomass/economic productivity is less than 20% of its potential (degraded land lying unused). 25-35% are not the usual threshold.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
items.s: Large-scale forest die-offs take place due to the biotic agent
items.x: Large-scale forest die-offs are driven by biotic agents such as insect pests and their pathogens (bark beetles, defoliators). Age, chemicals and water deficiency are not biotic. (Off-topic: forest ecology.)

items.s: In which of the following year, the Environment (Protection) Act was enacted in India?

items.x: The Environment (Protection) Act was enacted in 1986, after the Bhopal gas tragedy, to implement the Stockholm decisions.

o: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmer's Welfare
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

items.src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer in Sainik Welfare Service
items.s: First International Earth Summit was held at
items.x: The first Earth Summit (UN Conference on Environment and Development, June 1992) was held at Rio de Janeiro; it adopted the UNFCCC, CBD and Agenda 21. Paris hosted COP21 (2015), not the Earth Summit.

items.s:

items.x: Planting trees and cutting plastic protect natural resources – the environmental pillar of sustainable development (the others are economic and social).

items.src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer & Other Posts General St

o: Increasing the use of fossil fuels to boost economic growth
Prioritizing present economic needs over future environmental concerns
Reducing greenhouse gas emissions to ensure environmental sustainability
Ignoring biodiversity conservation in favor of urban expansion

o: Setting up of rain water harvesting systems
items.x: Unplanned waste generation wastes resources and pollutes, so it is not sustainable development. Crop rotation, solar energy and rainwater harvesting are sustainable practices. (Moved to 5:80.)

o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
items.x: The SDG India Index, which ranks States and UTs on sustainable development, is built by NITI Aayog (with MoSPI and the UN in India).

items.s: One of the United Nation's Millennium goals is to eradicate extreme poverty and hunger globally; today more than half of the extreme poor in the world live in
items.x: By World Bank estimates, more than half of the world's extremely poor live in Sub-Saharan Africa.

items.src: APPSC AEE (Civil), AMVI, Agriculture Officer and Other Posts
items.s: Sustainable Development Goals apply to
items.x: The SDGs (2030 Agenda, 2015) are universal and apply to all countries, developed and developing alike, unlike the MDGs, which targeted developing countries.

items.s: Which of the following is not true about SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT GOALs of UNO?
o: They encourage promotion of health, well being and prosperity for all
They promote sustainable cities and infrastructure.
They are legally binding on all member countries of UNO
items.x: The SDGs are a voluntary political agenda (2030 Agenda) and are not legally binding on UN members. They do promote health, innovation (Goal 9) and sustainable cities (Goal 11).

items.s: Which one of the following is one of the 17 sustainable development goals of UNO?
o: Reduce carbon emissions by 90 percent during the period of 15 years
Reduce global warming by 3 degrees centigrade in 5 years
Replace all appliances using green house gases in 15 years
Take urgent action to combat climate change and its impacts
items.x: SDG 13 is 'Take urgent action to combat climate change and its impacts'. The other options are invented numerical targets that are not SDGs.

items.s: Which is not part of the UNO's SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT GOALs on ecosystems?
items.x: SDG 15 (Life on Land) asks to use ecosystems sustainably, halt and reverse land degradation and halt biodiversity loss; it does not ask to halt biotechnology.

items.s: Which of the following policies and practices is most effective in achieving Sustainable Development?
o: Subsidizing fossil fuel industries to ensure lower energy costs for consumers.
Implementing carbon pricing to incentivize renewable energy investments.
Encouraging the use of single-use plastics to boost economic growth.
Promoting deforestation to create more land for agricultural activities.
items.x: Carbon pricing makes polluters pay and pushes investment into renewables; fossil subsidies, single-use plastics and deforestation work against sustainable development.

items.s: What is the formula of Ozone?
items.x: Ozone is triatomic oxygen, O3; O2 is ordinary oxygen and O4/O5 are not ozone.

items.s: — is/are responsible for ozone depletion.
items.x: Chlorofluorocarbons release chlorine in the stratosphere that destroys ozone; H2O2, CO and SO2 are not the ozone-depleting substances.

items.s: Which of the following refrigerants is the least toxic?
items.x: CFCs (freons) are non-toxic, non-flammable refrigerants (their problem is ozone depletion); SO2, methyl chloride and ammonia are toxic.

items.s: Which of the following chemicals, also known as C8, has been banned at the 9th Stockholm Convention held in Geneva?
items.x: COP-9 of the Stockholm Convention (Geneva, 2019) listed perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA, 'C8', used in making Teflon) in Annex A for elimination, with some exemptions, along with dicofol.
